The Continual Pursuit of Excellence
Welcome
The Raleigh School is a vibrant and ambitious primary school at the heart of our community, where every child is known, valued and supported to succeed.
We combine strong academic achievement with a warm, caring ethos shaped by our values of Respect, Resilience, Courage, Honesty and Unity. Our broad curriculum and rich extra‑curricular offer help children grow in confidence, curiosity and character.
We also welcome children aged 3–4 through our new pre‑school provision.
As part of the South Farnham Educational Trust, we work closely with partner schools while maintaining our own identity and commitment to every child. Read more..

Homework
We want our pupils to look forward to each school day. Spending an inordinate amount of time the previous evening doing homework is liable to dampen enthusiasm. Equally, there is a need for children to develop the habit of working away from school and to understand that learning does not only happen within school.
From their first term, the children are encouraged to take work home. This will often include spelling or further practice in a particular skill such as reading etc. As the children progress through the school, the amount of homework will increase, as will the nature of the tasks.
If you have any concerns about the amount or type of homework, please contact the class teacher as it is important that parents and teachers work together.

Mathletics
Mathletics is designed to target maths fluency within a rewarding, captivating and safe learning experience. All children are able to access a range of curriculum activities which are backed up by interactive tutorials and audio support.
Across the school, teachers will sometimes assign activities as part of the homework package.

Spelling Shed provides a safe, secure and engaging online world of learning for students to help them develop their spelling skills. There are a wide range of spelling games and activities based on a teacher-assigned word list. Rewards and certificates also keep students motivated. Look, cover, write, check – without the endless repetition.

ITT & ECT Partners
At The Raleigh School, we are proud to play an active role in developing the next generation of teachers. As a high-performing, inclusive school, we work in close partnership with SFET Teaching School Hub and South Farnham SCITT to support the delivery of their Initial Teacher Training (ITT) and Early Career Teacher (ECT) programmes.
Our commitment to teacher development is rooted in the belief that strong teaching transforms lives and that exceptional teachers are shaped through excellent training, mentoring and reflective practice.
To learn more about the excellent work of SFET Teaching School Hub and South Farnham SCITT, follow the links within this section.

Local Governing Body
The Raleigh School has been a proud member of the South Farnham Educational Trust since July 2017.
South Farnham Educational Trust is a Multi-Academy Trust established in January 2015 and led by South Farnham School.
The Trust Board delegates certain responsibilities to each school’s Local Governing Body, which has general oversight of the effective management and strategic direction of the school.
Our Local Governing Body brings together a range of skills, experience and perspectives to support and challenge the school effectively. Parent representatives play an important role within this structure, strengthening the partnership between home and school and contributing valuable insight into school life.
The Chair of Governors is Mr Giles Puckle who can be contacted via the school office.

Safeguarding
The Raleigh School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. We expect all staff, volunteers, and visitors to share this commitment.
Safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility. We have clear child protection policies and procedures in place, and all staff, including supply staff, volunteers, and governors, receive appropriate safeguarding training and guidance. Parents and carers are welcome to view all safeguarding-related policies in the School Policies section of our website.
We work closely with parents, carers and external agencies to safeguard children. Where concerns arise, we will usually discuss these with parents or carers at the earliest appropriate opportunity, unless we believe that doing so would place a child at further risk.
All staff, including teachers, support staff, volunteers, and governors, receive regular safeguarding training and updates. This ensures that everyone working in the school understands their responsibilities, knows how to recognise concerns and is confident in how to report them appropriately.
Designated Safeguarding Leads (DSLs) are members of staff who have specific responsibility for safeguarding and child protection within the school. They provide advice and guidance to staff, respond to concerns and work closely with families and external agencies to ensure children are kept safe.
Reporting a concern
If you are concerned about a child’s welfare, please record your concern, including any observations or conversations, and report it to a Designated Safeguarding Lead as soon as possible on the same day.
Do not investigate concerns yourself.
If your concern relates to the behaviour or actions of a member of staff, this should be reported in confidence to a Designated Safeguarding Lead. The matter will be referred to the Headteacher, or to the Chair of Governors if the concern relates to the Headteacher, and managed in line with statutory guidance.

Before & After School Care
The contact number for Earlybirds & Shipmates outside of school office opening hours is 01483 281903
We are delighted to be able to offer a high quality wrap around child care provision for children at The Raleigh.
Earlybirds is our breakfast club which runs from 7:40am until 8:40am. Children attending are provided with breakfast (typically cereal, toast, a drink and fruit). At 08:40 children move from the club into the main playground to begin the school day.
Shipmates is our after school club which runs from 3:15pm until 5:45pm. Children attending are provided with a light snack (typically wraps, crumpets, cheese, ham, salad items, a drink and fruit.
Booking and payment must be made in advance via the School Office. Please see our Prospectus below for more detailed information.
